test_policy.notes: Freshman page: SAT/ACT is test optional, but scores are required for Lander academic scholarships. Applicants are evaluated on course prerequisites, high school GPA and SAT/ACT scores if submitted. No minimum GPA is printed. The international page does not require SAT/ACT; an SAT verbal 450 or ACT verbal 18 is one optional way to show English proficiency.

requirements.notes: Online application on Lander's site (no Common App listed). International applicants need official school records in the original language plus certified English translations, a course-by-course evaluation from a NACES-certified service (applicant pays), an affidavit of support stating the amount and length of funds, and English proficiency evidence; credentials must arrive at least 6 months before the term. Application fee is not stated on the admissions pages. Mandatory student health insurance applies after enrollment.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Fall June 15, spring Nov. 1, summer March 15 (international). Printed without a year; treated as fall 2027. The same page asks for credentials at least 6 months before the term, which is earlier than June 15 for an August start. Domestic freshmen apply by Aug. 1 on a rolling basis.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Not required if English is the official native language, ENGL 101 and 102 were completed at a U.S. regionally accredited college, SAT verbal 450 or ACT verbal 18 is submitted, or the applicant holds a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution. TOEIC 600 is also accepted. Lander contracts with ELS Language Centers for English instruction; the ESL page says students can be admitted to Lander on completing ELS program level 112. Conditional admission is not described.

english.notes: Institution code 5363. The page does not give a separate 1-6 scale minimum.

cost.notes: From the fee sheet for fall and spring (Aug-May, full time 12-18 credits): tuition $10,700 plus out-of-state fee $9,600 (international students pay $20,300); university fees $1,200 and auxiliary fee $300 (required fees $1,500). International extras $1,800 = required health insurance (average) $1,500 plus a one-time $300 matriculation fee. Living: room and board $12,436, books $500, transportation $2,400, personal $2,000 (other $4,400). The sheet totals $40,936 for 9 months; the column labels in the PDF text are misaligned, so each line was matched by arithmetic (the lines sum to the printed totals). Summer terms are extra.

aid.notes: Freshman academic scholarship tiers (President's, Trustee's, Provost's, Dean's) pay $500-$6,000/year plus a $4,000-$8,000 tuition abatement for out-of-state students, based on ACT/SAT and a 3.5 weighted GPA (or 3.0 unweighted); apply by May 1 for automatic consideration. The scholarship page does not say whether international students qualify, and scores are required to be considered. A departmental International Student Scholarship (accounting, management/marketing, finance/economics emphasis) exists with no amount published. International students are not eligible for federal aid.

sat.note: The international admissions pages do not print a numeric SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search.

act.note: The international admissions pages do not print an ACT code; look it up at act.org.
